{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-nj-d","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"98c600470c24a51d6d63b708d2bd2b07babfea4da97b5bd8f052d3c06994acf0","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-nj-class-d:lineage:46","source_registry_sha256":"057b72c7c679c997f56ae00ef97a6b14dbe264551f4121b9bf67b0457d9cf7c1","source_liveness_sha256":"1ca7bfbb9e3c0a6b19e5e808ecab6fe8329f3b4799e394abc260d65c1d6513e7"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Driver privilege and penalties: suspension, DUI and underage penalties, breath-test refusal, ignition interlock, IDRC and moving violation penalties","heading":"C — Driver privilege and penalties: the driving privilege and suspension reasons, DUI and underage drinking penalties, implied consent and breath-test refusal, ignition interlock terms, the Intoxicated Driver Resource Center, and fines for unsafe and reckless driving, open containers, snow and ice, doubled-fine zones and police stops","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Driver privilege and penalties: the driving privilege and suspension reasons, DUI and underage drinking penalties, implied consent and breath-test refusal, ignition interlock terms, the Intoxicated Driver Resource Center, and fines for unsafe and reckless driving, open containers, snow and ice, doubled-fine zones and police stops
Knowledge domain: why New Jersey treats driving as a privilege that can be suspended, the mandatory penalties for adult and underage drunk driving, what implied consent means and what refusing a breath test costs, when an ignition interlock is required and for how long, how the Intoxicated Driver Resource Center works, and the fines tied to common moving violations.

FACT_ID: sec11-F01 | anchor: A01
Driving is a privilege rather than a right, and state law allows or requires suspension for certain violations, on top of possible fines and imprisonment. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0124]

FACT_ID: sec11-F02 | anchor: A01
A habitual offender is a driver whose license has been suspended three times within three years. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0124]

FACT_ID: sec11-F03 | anchor: A01
Grounds for losing the privilege include unanswered or unpaid parking tickets, driving while suspended, no proof of insurance, physical or mental disqualification, drug or alcohol use, traffic violations, fault in a fatal crash and ignoring an MVC notice. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0124]

FACT_ID: sec11-F04 | anchor: A01
The MVC Chief Administrator may order a re-examination of a problem driver to help decide whether to suspend driving privileges. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0124]

FACT_ID: sec11-F05 | anchor: A01
In New Jersey a person must be at least 21 to buy, possess or drink alcohol, and adults who supply alcohol to underage people also face serious consequences. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0124]

FACT_ID: sec11-F06 | anchor: A02
A person under 21 who buys or drinks alcohol where alcohol is licensed for sale may be fined $500 and lose their license for a time. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0125]

FACT_ID: sec11-F07 | anchor: A02
If the underage person has no license yet, the suspension begins on the date they first become eligible for one, and an alcohol education or treatment program may be required. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0125]

FACT_ID: sec11-F08 | anchor: A02
For a first DUI with a BAC of 0.08 percent but under 0.10 percent, the fine is $250 to $400, with 12 to 48 hours at an IDRC and up to 30 days in jail. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0125]

FACT_ID: sec11-F09 | anchor: A02
The IDRC charges $264 when the program lasts 12 hours and $321 when it lasts 48 hours. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0125]

FACT_ID: sec11-F10 | anchor: A02
A first DUI offense also carries an annual surcharge of $1,000 for three years. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0125]

FACT_ID: sec11-F11 | anchor: A02
For a first DUI with a BAC of 0.10 percent or higher, the fine rises to $300 to $500. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0125]

FACT_ID: sec11-F12 | anchor: A03
For an underage first offense with a BAC from 0.01 up to under 0.08 percent, the license is suspended 30 to 90 days, starting on the later of eligibility or conviction. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0126]

FACT_ID: sec11-F13 | anchor: A03
An underage first offense also brings 15 to 30 days of community service and either an IDRC or an alcohol education and highway safety program. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0126]

FACT_ID: sec11-F14 | anchor: A04
Under New Jersey's implied consent law, simply driving on New Jersey roads means agreeing to a breath test by police or hospital staff after an arrest for intoxicated driving. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0129]

FACT_ID: sec11-F15 | anchor: A04
A driver who refuses the breath test is detained and taken to a hospital, where staff may draw blood. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0129]

FACT_ID: sec11-F16 | anchor: A04
Refusing a breath test carries a violation surcharge of $1,000 a year for three years. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0129]

FACT_ID: sec11-F17 | anchor: A04
A refusal conviction tied to a first offense means losing driving privileges until an ignition interlock device is installed. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0129]

FACT_ID: sec11-F18 | anchor: A04
An ignition interlock device has a built-in breathalyzer that stops the vehicle from starting when the driver's BAC is above 0.05 percent. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0129]

FACT_ID: sec11-F19 | anchor: A04
After a first DUI with a BAC of 0.08 to under 0.10 percent, the interlock stays installed for three months from restoration of driving privileges. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0129]

FACT_ID: sec11-F20 | anchor: A04
After a first DUI with a BAC of 0.10 to under 0.15 percent, the interlock is required for seven months to one year after restoration. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0129]

FACT_ID: sec11-F21 | anchor: A04
After a first DUI at 0.15 percent or higher, the interlock is required during the suspension and for 12 to 15 months after restoration. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0129]

FACT_ID: sec11-F22 | anchor: A04
After a second or later DUI or refusal offense, the interlock is required during the suspension and for two to four years after restoration. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0129]

FACT_ID: sec11-F23 | anchor: A05
For offenses on or after February 19, 2024, a person arrested for certain alcohol offenses may install an interlock voluntarily before conviction, which may reduce fines and the suspension period. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0130]

FACT_ID: sec11-F24 | anchor: A05
Anyone charged with an alcohol-related traffic offense must be detained at an IDRC, where offenders take an alcohol and highway safety education program and are evaluated for treatment needs. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0130]

FACT_ID: sec11-F25 | anchor: A05
Each of New Jersey's 21 counties has an IDRC for first- and third-time offenders, while second-time offenders go to one of three regional IDRCs. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0130]

FACT_ID: sec11-F26 | anchor: A05
Offenders found to need treatment are referred for a program of at least 16 weeks, and satisfactory participation is a condition for getting licensed again. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0130]

FACT_ID: sec11-F27 | anchor: A05
An unsafe driving conviction is fined $50 to $150 the first time, $100 to $250 the second, and $200 to $500 for a third or later offense, plus a $250 court surcharge each time. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0130]

FACT_ID: sec11-F28 | anchor: A05
A third or later unsafe driving offense within five years of the previous one also adds 4 motor vehicle penalty points. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0130]

FACT_ID: sec11-F29 | anchor: A06
A first reckless driving offense can bring up to 60 days in jail, a fine of $50 to $200, or both, and points are also assessed. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0131]

FACT_ID: sec11-F30 | anchor: A06
Carrying an open or unsealed alcohol container, or an unsealed cannabis item, in the passenger area is fined $200 the first time and $250 or 10 days of community service after that. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0131]

FACT_ID: sec11-F31 | anchor: A06
If ice flies off a private vehicle and causes death, injury or property damage, the driver faces a fine of $200 to $1,000 each time, and commercial owners and operators face $500 to $1,500. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0131]

FACT_ID: sec11-F32 | anchor: A06
Failing to clear snow or ice from a vehicle before driving carries a $25 to $75 fine even if none of it comes loose. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0131]

FACT_ID: sec11-F33 | anchor: A06
In a 65 mph zone, speeding 10 mph or more over the limit, or certain other moving violations, means doubled fines. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0131]

FACT_ID: sec11-F34 | anchor: A06
A driver who ignores a police officer's request to light up the driver's compartment during a stop faces a $50 fine. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0131]

Misconceptions: refusing a breath test does not avoid penalties, it carries its own surcharge and interlock requirement; an underage driver does not need to reach the adult limit to be charged; having no license yet does not cancel an underage suspension, it simply starts later; clearing snow is required even if nothing would have flown off.
Mnemonics: interlock ladder after a first DUI is three months, then seven to twelve months, then twelve to fifteen months as BAC climbs; the interlock trips above point-oh-five; three suspensions in three years makes a habitual offender; doubled fines in work zones and sixty-five zones.
Glossary: implied consent means agreeing to a breath test just by driving on New Jersey roads; ignition interlock device means a breathalyzer wired to the ignition that blocks starting after drinking; IDRC means Intoxicated Driver Resource Center, where alcohol offenders are detained and evaluated; habitual offender means a driver suspended three times in three years; surcharge means a yearly MVC charge on top of court fines.
Dynamic facts: fines, fees, surcharges and interlock terms in this chapter are set by statute and can change; confirm current amounts on the official MVC website.
